prompt: Some people think that team sports prepare children for work life, but others think individual sports are better. Discuss both sides and give your opinion.
essay:
It is often argued that participating in team sports can prepare children for their future careers, while others believe that individual activities are more beneficial. Both perspectives have clear advantages; however, I believe that team-based sports provide better preparation for professional life.

On the one hand, individual sports can be beneficial for several reasons. The main advantage is clear: they teach children to become independent and self-disciplined. This is important because young athletes must set their own goals, manage their time, and remain motivated without depending on teammates. In addition, individual activities encourage personal responsibility, which can lead to greater confidence. For example, a young swimmer may practise every morning without being reminded by others; as a result, the child can develop strong self-discipline. Therefore, it is understandable why some people support this view.

On the other hand, I believe that team sports offer greater benefits. The main reason is clear: they help children develop important communication skills. Not only does this improve their ability to work with others, but it also teaches them how to share responsibilities. Moreover, young players learn to deal with disagreements and respect different opinions. For instance, football players must communicate and cooperate during a match; consequently, they develop skills that can later be useful in the workplace. Therefore, I consider this approach more practical and effective.

In conclusion, individual sports certainly offer independence and self-discipline; however, I believe that team sports are preferable because they develop communication and cooperation skills. Overall, this approach is likely to prepare children more effectively for their future careers.
